section: Pass and fail criteria, at N=100
note: The second rung. Sealed before the N=100 run, with the N=10 record (results/n10) as the only prior. predictions.json is the N=10 rung and is not edited; this file is this rung's, as E15 does with predictions-metal.json. The substantive claim is N100-P10: N=10 found no queueing anywhere, and at N=100 against ONE sbx-worker replica something is expected to queue. If N100-P10 is falsified -- if 100 concurrent users are still as cheap as one -- that is the more interesting outcome and it is reported as falsified, not rewritten.

setting.cluster: OpenShift ykt1, namespace moca-sbx, profile sandbox, control plane main-3b53f15
setting.workers: 1 sbx-worker replica, unchanged from the N=10 rung
setting.users: test:1..test:100, all in flight at once (concurrency 100)
setting.driver_host: 18 cores, 64 GB, macOS arm64, over the public Route
setting.driver_host_note: 100 concurrent node processes at ~93 MB resident is ~9.3 GB, so the driver host is not expected to be the limit. If it is, the rung measures the laptop and must be re-run with --concurrency.

predictions.claim: All 100 users complete the whole lifecycle with no failure. Nothing in the N=10 rung suggested a per-user limit, and SH_TEST_USERS=1000 authorises the range.
login p90 stays under 2500 ms: 100 near-simultaneous logins against a single control-plane pod, each signing a token.
run_id p90 stays under 20000 ms. This is where queueing at one worker should land, and the bar is set wide because the N=10 rung gives no evidence about where the knee is.
100 concurrent users still beat 100 sequential ones by a wide margin: wall clock stays under 180000 ms, against roughly 904000 ms sequential at the N=10 per-user p50.
The driver runs on a free-threaded interpreter.

Unlike N=10, N=100 does NOT stay flat: wall clock is at least twice the N=10 wall of 9138 ms, because 100 concurrent run calls share one sbx-worker replica. A directional claim, and the one worth sealing: if it fails, 100 users cost what one costs and the worker is nowhere near its limit.
